boundaries.trigger: Every `$(...)` / backtick substitution evaluated with the default runner runs `/bin/sh -c <text>`.
boundaries.policy: UNEXPECTED FINDING, not a conditional fallback: the production implementation of command substitution hands the substituted text to the system POSIX shell, so the nested command's semantics come from /bin/sh. Contradicts the replacement architecture; requires an explicit pre-1.0 decision. Not changed in Slice 2.
boundaries.notes: Category D is the nearest of the six fixed categories (automatic hand-off to a legacy shell); it is always on and has no switch. The fuzz harness replaces this runner with a fake.

boundaries.trigger: `run_script FILE` where FILE's own shebang names bash, sh or zsh.
boundaries.policy: The script explicitly requests the interpreter. Interpreter is optional; absence yields a controlled status 127 and no other shell is substituted. Direct `pysh FILE` ignores the shebang (native_only=True).
boundaries.notes: Not an automatic fallback: PySH language semantics are not handed off; the script asked for another interpreter.
